rule: When offering appointment times to a patient, list no more than three options in a single message.
why: This prevents overwhelming patients and ensures compliance with the limit on offered options.

rule: When presenting available appointment times, always select and display up to three options in each message, even if more are available.
why: This ensures patients are not overwhelmed and complies with the limit on offered options.

rule: When offering appointment times, list no more than 3 options in a single message, even if more are available. If needed, offer additional options only after the patient declines all previous ones.
why: This prevents overwhelming the patient and ensures compliance with the limit on offered options.
reasons: targets did not improve (6 -> 6 passing trials)

rule: When multiple appointment times are available, offer only the first 3 options in your reply. If the patient declines all, offer up to 3 more, repeating until options are exhausted or one is accepted.
why: This prevents overwhelming the patient and ensures no more than 3 options are presented at once, matching the requirement.

rule: If a patient uses an ambiguous date like 'next Wednesday', clarify which specific date they mean before offering appointment times or booking.
why: The assistant booked an appointment for the wrong date when the patient's request was ambiguous, leading to an incorrect booking.
